data.text: Now that you understand the basics, let's explore **practical HOC implementations** for common scenarios. Each example below solves a real problem you might face in a production React application.
The `withLoading` HOC adds a loading state to any component. It accepts an `isLoading` prop and shows a fallback UI while data is being fetched.

data.title: withLoading
data.content: A reusable HOC that shows a loading indicator

data.text: The `withLogger` HOC logs props and lifecycle events for debugging. It is invaluable during development to understand what data a component receives and when it re-renders.

data.title: withLogger
data.content: An HOC that logs props and render events

data.text: The `withUserData` HOC fetches user data and injects it as a prop. This keeps your component focused on display while the HOC handles the data-fetching concern.

data.title: withUserData
data.content: Fetching user data and injecting it into a component

data.text: Different HOCs solve different problems. Here is a quick comparison of common use cases and when to apply each pattern.

data.title: Static Methods
data.text: HOCs do not copy static methods automatically. If your wrapped component defines static helpers (like `getInitialProps`), use `hoist-non-react-statics` to copy them to the enhanced component.

items.text: Use the `with` prefix for HOC names (e.g., `withLoading`, `withAuth`)
Set `displayName` on the returned component for better debugging
Pass through all original props using the spread operator
Avoid mutating the original component - always return a new one
Compose unrelated HOCs separately instead of nesting deeply
Use `hoist-non-react-statics` if static methods must be preserved
Keep HOCs focused on a single responsibility

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: withLoading wraps components to show a loading fallback
withLogger helps debug prop changes and renders
withUserData fetches data and injects it as a prop
HOCs should be focused and composable
data.takeaway: Practical HOCs solve real problems while keeping components clean.

data.title: Create a withFetch HOC
data.description: Build a `withFetch` HOC that accepts a URL, fetches data from that endpoint, and provides `data`, `isLoading`, and `error` props to the wrapped component.
steps: Define the HOC function signature with generic typing for the response data
Use `useState` and `useEffect` inside the HOC to perform the fetch
Handle loading, success, and error states gracefully
Pass the fetched data, loading flag, and error to the wrapped component
Clean up the effect if the component unmounts or the URL changes
data.expectedOutcome: A reusable `withFetch` HOC that works with any API endpoint and response shape.
